title: VPC Topology Gardener: subnet allocator, NAT/IGW selector, endpoint routing and upgrade sentinel
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Implement a single, opinionated Terraform module (vpc-topology-gardener) to manage VPC topology for Redwood Private deployments. The module will provision AZ-aware subnets, provide a pluggable NAT/IGW abstraction, create and manage interface/gateway VPC endpoints with endpoint policies, and maintain route-table orchestration. It must include upgrade-safety primitives (canary terraform plans, state-safe renames), and a health-checking surface that reports topology drift and endpoint reachability to our observability stack.

Scope:
- Core module: subnet allocation patterns (public/private/utility), route tables, NAT gateway autoscaling pattern, egress IGW paths, and optional NAT Gateway proxy (for cost/capacity shapes).
- Endpoints: create interface endpoints and gateway endpoints per service (S3, Dynamo, KMS, ECR), attach endpoint policies, and wire routes for gateway endpoints.
- Routing: deterministic route priorities, explicit blackhole detection and reconciliation hooks.
- Upgrades: module-level versioning, canary apply flow (non-prod -> limited-prod -> full-prod), automatic plan validation checks, and an upgrade sentinel that gates destructive changes.
- Health checks: synthetic connectivity probes (VPC reachability checks, endpoint DNS resolution, NAT metric anomalies), route-table drift checks, and alert rules that map to Runbook.
- Observability: emit CloudWatch / Datadog metrics and create a default dashboard template.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Single module vs. micro-modules: chosen single cohesive module with small sub-modules to reduce copy/paste and ensure consistent tagging while allowing customers to opt-out for particular capabilities.
- NAT vs. Proxy: supporting both NAT Gateway and an optional central egress proxy gives cost flexibility. Default is NAT but proxy is an opt-in advanced mode.
- Endpoint policies: applying strict endpoint policies by default will reduce blast radius but increases maintenance; default to permissive templates and provide hardened policy examples.
- State migration: we will avoid renaming critical resources; where rename is required we will provide a migration plan script and explicit terraform state mv commands in the docs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Module creates AZ-balanced subnet groups and route tables in a sample test account without manual overrides.
- Interface and gateway endpoints provisioned with configurable policies and are reachable from an attached test instance.
- Upgrade sentinel blocks any apply that would delete or rename internet-facing route tables unless an explicit flag and migration doc are provided.
- Health checks detect and report: (a) missing routes (blackhole), (b) endpoint DNS resolution failures, (c) NAT gateway high error-rate based on CloudWatch metrics.
- CI terraform plan check runs and fails on accidental wide-scope deletions; PR must include a passing plan scan job.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge module into infra-modules repo behind feature flag.
2) Deploy to staging accounts and run self-healing test harness (see test links).
3) Canary apply to a single non-critical prod VPC (limited subnet subset).
4) Validate dashboards and alerts for 72 hours.
5) Gradual ramp to all production VPCs; capture any manual steps in the runbook.

Testing & validation:
- Unit: terraform validate + tflint + custom policy checks (regula).
- Integration: terraform apply in ephemeral accounts created by ci/test harness; run connectivity tests from bastion and k8s node.
- Chaos: simulate NAT gateway failure and ensure autoscale/failover triggers and alerts.

Docs & artifacts: see docs_links and prs fields below for design doc, runbook, and draft policies.

Security: KMS-protected state bucket and least-privilege IAM role usage is required. Endpoint policies include examples for least-privilege templates. Security review required before GA.
